issues.description: The getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field is inconsistent between the template and the solution. In the template StockIngredient class the getter is named getIngredientName(), and the template Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getIngredientName(). In the solution repository the getter is named getName(), and the solution Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getName(). This mismatch between template and solution (different public method names for the same data) is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about the expected API and cause integration issues if they follow one artifact while comparing to the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the public getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field across all artifacts. Either rename the template's getIngredientName() to getName() and update Stock.findStockIngredient() to call getName(), or rename the solution's getName() to getIngredientName() and update its Stock.findStockIngredient() accordingly. Ensure the problem statement mentions the chosen getter name (or leaves it unspecified) so all code artifacts use the same API.

issues.description: The getter for the ingredient name is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template defines StockIngredient.getIngredientName() while the solution defines StockIngredient.getName(). Corresponding usages in Stock.findStockIngredient() also call the different getter names. This disparity refers to the same conceptual entity (the ingredient's name) but uses two different identifiers across template and solution, which can confuse students implementing or comparing their code to the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name consistent across template and solution. Prefer a standard getter name matching the field (e.g., getName()). Update the template to rename getIngredientName() to getName() and adjust all calls (e.g., in Stock.findStockIngredient) accordingly — or conversely make the solution use getIngredientName() if that name is preferred. Ensure both repositories use the same identifier.
